q: The Swaraj Party, founded in 1923, was led by:
e: The Swaraj Party was founded in 1923 by C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru to enter the legislative councils, and C. R. Das was its principal leader.

q: Who was the first Indian woman to preside over a session of the Indian National Congress?
e: Sarojini Naidu presided over the Kanpur session of the Indian National Congress in 1925, becoming the first Indian woman to preside over a Congress session.

q: The ancient university of Nalanda was located in the present-day State of:
e: The ancient university of Nalanda stood near Rajgir in present-day Bihar and flourished for centuries as a great centre of Buddhist learning.

q: The famous Iron Pillar at Mehrauli (Delhi) is associated with the reign of:
e: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar bears an inscription of a king named Chandra, identified with the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II.

q: Which Gupta ruler is known as the 'Napoleon of India'?
e: Samudragupta is known as the "Napoleon of India" because of his extensive military conquests across northern and southern India, recorded in the Allahabad Pillar inscription.

q: The Taj Mahal at Agra was built by the Mughal emperor:
e: The Taj Mahal at Agra was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal.

q: Razia Sultan was a ruler of the:
e: Razia Sultan, daughter of Iltutmish, was the only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, reigning from 1236 to 1240.

q: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by:
e: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by the brothers Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty.

q: The Battle of Khanwa (1527) was fought between Babur and:
e: At the Battle of Khanwa in 1527, Babur defeated Rana Sanga of Mewar, consolidating Mughal power a year after the victory at Panipat.

q: The Nathu La pass is located in the State of:
e: Nathu La is a mountain pass in Sikkim connecting India with Tibet (China); it was reopened for border trade in 2006 after decades of closure.

q: Jim Corbett National Park, the first national park of India, is located in:
e: Jim Corbett National Park, established in 1936 as India's first national park, is located in Uttarakhand and is famous for its tiger population.

q: Kaziranga National Park in Assam is world-famous for the:
e: Kaziranga National Park in Assam holds the world's largest population of the Indian one-horned rhinoceros, for which it is world-famous.

q: The Gir National Park in Gujarat is the natural home of the:
e: Gir National Park in Gujarat is the only natural home in the world of the Asiatic lion.

q: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bengal'?
e: The Damodar river was known as the "Sorrow of Bengal" because of its frequent devastating floods in West Bengal; the Kosi is similarly the "Sorrow of Bihar".

q: In Arunachal Pradesh, the Brahmaputra river is known by the name:
e: In Arunachal Pradesh the Brahmaputra is known as the Siang (Dihang); it is called Tsangpo in Tibet and Jamuna in Bangladesh.

q: The capital of Nagaland is:
e: Kohima is the capital of Nagaland and is also remembered for the fierce Battle of Kohima fought in 1944 during the Second World War.

q: The Jog Falls, among the highest waterfalls in India, are located on the river:
e: Jog Falls, among the highest waterfalls in India, are formed by the Sharavati river in Karnataka.

q: The Reserve Bank of India was established in the year:
e: The Reserve Bank of India was established on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, as the central bank of the country.

q: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised in the year:
e: The Reserve Bank of India, originally a shareholders' bank, was nationalised with effect from 1 January 1949.

q: The one-rupee note in India is issued by the:

options.B: Ministry of Finance, Government of India
options.D: Securities and Exchange Board of India

e: The one-rupee note is issued by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, and bears the signature of the Finance Secretary, unlike other currency notes issued by the RBI.

q: 'Fiscal deficit' of the Government means:

options.A: The difference between revenue receipts and revenue expenditure
options.B: The difference between exports and imports
options.C: The excess of imports over exports
options.D: Total expenditure minus total receipts other than borrowings

e: Fiscal deficit means total expenditure minus total receipts other than borrowings; it thus indicates the total borrowing requirement of the Government for the year.

q: The SI unit of electric current is the:
e: The ampere is the SI unit of electric current; the volt measures potential difference, the ohm resistance and the watt power.

q: Boyle's law relates, for a given mass of gas at constant temperature:
e: Boyle's law states that for a given mass of gas at constant temperature, the pressure is inversely proportional to its volume.

q: The laws of planetary motion were propounded by:
e: Johannes Kepler propounded the three laws of planetary motion, describing the elliptical orbits in which planets move around the Sun.

q: The deficiency of Vitamin D in children causes:
e: Deficiency of Vitamin D causes rickets in children, a disease marked by soft, weak and deformed bones; in adults the deficiency leads to osteomalacia.

q: The Thomas Cup is the world team championship in:
e: The Thomas Cup is the world men's team championship in badminton, contested by national teams since 1949.

q: The Davis Cup is associated with the game of:
e: The Davis Cup is the premier international team competition in men's tennis, played between national teams.

q: The first modern Olympic Games were held in 1896 at:
e: The first modern Olympic Games were held in 1896 at Athens in Greece, the home of the ancient Olympic Games.

q: Kathakali is a classical dance form of the State of:
e: Kathakali, the dance-drama distinguished by elaborate make-up, costumes and facial expressions, is the classical dance form of Kerala.

q: The Sun Temple at Konark is located in the State of:
e: The Sun Temple at Konark, built in the form of a giant chariot of the Sun God drawn by horses, is located in Odisha.

q: The headquarters of the South Coast Railway, the newest zonal railway of Indian Railways, is located at:
e: The headquarters of the South Coast Railway, the newest zonal railway of Indian Railways, is located at Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh.

q: The 'LHB' coaches widely used by Indian Railways are named after:
e: LHB coaches are named after Linke Hofmann Busch of Germany, whose coach design was adopted by Indian Railways for safer and faster passenger trains.

q: The first Vande Bharat Express, flagged off in February 2019, was introduced between:
e: The first Vande Bharat Express, flagged off in February 2019, was introduced between New Delhi and Varanasi.

q: The first Tejas Express, introduced in May 2017, ran between:
e: The first Tejas Express, introduced in May 2017, ran between Mumbai (CSMT) and Karmali in Goa.

q: The first Garib Rath Express, introduced in 2005 for affordable air-conditioned travel, ran between:
e: The first Garib Rath Express, offering affordable air-conditioned travel to common passengers, was introduced between Amritsar and Saharsa.

q: India's first air-conditioned Double Decker Express, introduced in 2011, ran between:
e: India's first air-conditioned Double Decker Express, introduced in 2011, ran between Howrah and Dhanbad.

q: Duronto Express trains were originally introduced as:

options.A: Trains with only sleeper class coaches
options.C: Point-to-point trains with no commercial stoppages en route

e: Duronto Express trains were originally introduced as point-to-point services running from origin to destination with no commercial stoppages en route.

q: Antyodaya Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.B: Trains with only AC first class coaches
options.D: Superfast trains composed entirely of unreserved general second-class coaches

e: Antyodaya Express trains are superfast services composed entirely of unreserved general second-class coaches, intended for the benefit of the common passenger.

q: Humsafar Express trains are characterised by:

options.A: Fully air-conditioned three-tier coaches with enhanced passenger amenities

e: Humsafar Express trains are characterised by fully air-conditioned three-tier coaches fitted with enhanced passenger amenities such as CCTV cameras, bio-toilets and information displays.

q: The full form of IRCTC is:

options.A: Indian Railway Catering and Transport Corporation
options.B: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation
options.C: Indian Rail Commerce and Tourism Company
options.D: International Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation

e: IRCTC stands for Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation, the railway public sector undertaking that handles catering, tourism and online ticket booking.

q: The full form of CRIS is:
e: CRIS stands for Centre for Railway Information Systems, the organisation that designs, develops and maintains the information technology systems of Indian Railways.

q: The full form of CONCOR is:
e: CONCOR stands for Container Corporation of India Limited, the railway undertaking that operates container terminals and container freight services across the country.

q: The full form of DFCCIL is:

options.A: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited
options.B: Delhi Freight Corridor Company of India Limited
options.C: Dedicated Freight Container Corporation of India Limited
options.D: Direct Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited

e: DFCCIL stands for Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited, the special purpose company building and operating the dedicated freight corridors.

q: The Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation (MRVC) is primarily responsible for:

options.B: Executing suburban railway infrastructure projects in the Mumbai region

e: The Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation is primarily responsible for executing suburban railway infrastructure projects in the Mumbai region under the Mumbai Urban Transport Project.

q: The full form of RLDA, a statutory authority under the Ministry of Railways, is:
e: RLDA stands for Rail Land Development Authority, the statutory authority under the Ministry of Railways for commercial development of vacant railway land.

q: USBRL, the rail link project in Jammu and Kashmir, stands for:
e: USBRL stands for Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link, the project that extended the rail line through the mountains to connect the Kashmir valley with the national network.

q: The full form of RITES is:

options.A: Rail India Technical and Economic Service
options.B: Railway Institute of Technical and Engineering Services
options.C: Rail Infrastructure and Transport Export Services
options.D: Research Institute of Transport and Engineering Sciences

e: RITES stands for Rail India Technical and Economic Service (now RITES Limited), the undertaking providing engineering and transport consultancy services in India and abroad.

q: The single integrated helpline number of Indian Railways for enquiries, assistance and grievance redressal is:
e: 139 is the single integrated helpline number of Indian Railways for enquiries, assistance, security help and grievance redressal, absorbing several earlier helpline numbers.

q: NTES, which provides real-time information about train running status, stands for:
e: NTES stands for National Train Enquiry System, the system that provides real-time information about the running status of trains to passengers.

q: Which is the only metro rail system in India that functions as a zonal railway under the Ministry of Railways?
e: Kolkata Metro is the only metro rail system in India that functions as a zonal railway under the Ministry of Railways; other metros are run by separate metro corporations.

q: Who among the following is regarded as the 'Father of Indian Railways'?
e: Lord Dalhousie, the Governor-General whose Railway Minute of 1853 laid the foundation of railway development in India, is regarded as the Father of Indian Railways.

q: The first passenger train of India in 1853 was run by which railway company?

options.C: Bombay, Baroda and Central India Railway

e: The first passenger train of India in 1853, between Bombay and Thane, was run by the Great Indian Peninsula Railway company.

q: Which was the first zonal railway formed after Independence, in April 1951?
e: Southern Railway, formed on 14 April 1951 by merging the southern railway companies, was the first zonal railway created after Independence.

q: The first train in India in 1853 started its journey from which station in Bombay?
e: The first train journey of 1853 started from Bori Bunder station in Bombay and terminated at Thane.

q: The first train journey of 1853 between Bombay and Thane covered a distance of about:
e: The first train journey of 1853 between Bombay (Bori Bunder) and Thane covered a distance of about 34 km.

q: The earliest railway line in India, the Red Hill Railroad of 1837 near Madras, was built mainly for carrying:
e: The Red Hill Railroad of 1837 near Madras, among the earliest railway lines in India, was built mainly for carrying granite stones used in road work.

q: The computerised Passenger Reservation System (PRS) was first introduced in the year 1986 at:
e: The computerised Passenger Reservation System (PRS) was first introduced in 1986 at New Delhi, beginning the computerisation of railway ticket reservations in India.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Government Railway Police (GRP) is a part of the State Police and is responsible for law and order and crime control in railway premises and trains.
2. The Railway Protection Force (RPF) is responsible for the protection and security of railway property.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Government Railway Police is a part of the State Police responsible for law and order and crime control in railway premises and trains, while the Railway Protection Force protects railway property.

q: In railway freight operations, 'demurrage' charges are levied for:

options.A: Detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed for loading or unloading
options.D: Booking of goods in excess of the permissible weight

e: Demurrage charges are levied for detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed for loading or unloading, so that railway stock is not held up unnecessarily.

q: In railway goods sheds, 'wharfage' charges are levied when:

options.A: Wagons are detained beyond free time
options.B: Goods are not removed from the railway premises within the prescribed free time
options.C: Goods are loaded in open wagons
options.D: Consignments are booked on 'to pay' basis

e: Wharfage charges are levied when goods are not removed from the railway premises within the prescribed free time after their arrival at the goods shed.

q: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway is built to which track gauge?

options.D: Narrow gauge of 2 feet 6 inches (762 mm)

e: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway is built to the narrow gauge of 2 feet (610 mm), a light gauge suited to its steep hill gradients and sharp curves.

q: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway is built to which track gauge?

options.C: Narrow gauge of 2 feet 6 inches (762 mm)

e: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway is built to metre gauge (1,000 mm) and uses a rack-and-pinion arrangement on its steep gradient section.

q: In locomotive class designations of Indian Railways such as WAP-7, the first letter 'W' indicates:
e: In locomotive class designations such as WAP-7, the first letter indicates the track gauge; "W" stands for broad gauge, derived from "wide".

q: In the locomotive class WAP-7, the letter 'A' indicates:
e: In the locomotive class WAP-7, the letter "A" indicates AC electric traction; the following "P" denotes passenger service.

q: The Golden Rock Railway Workshop of Indian Railways is located at:
e: The Golden Rock Railway Workshop of Indian Railways is located at Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) in Tamil Nadu.

q: The Rail Wheel Plant of Indian Railways is located at Bela in which State?
e: The Rail Wheel Plant of Indian Railways is located at Bela in the Saran district of Bihar.

q: The 'Lifeline Express' run on Indian Railways is famous as:

options.A: The world's first hospital on a train
options.C: The first train with a pantry car

e: The Lifeline Express is famous as the world's first hospital on a train, carrying doctors and medical facilities to remote rural areas.

q: The Samjhauta Express was a train service linking India with:
e: The Samjhauta Express was a train service linking India with Pakistan, running between Delhi and Lahore via the Attari border.

q: The Maitree Express runs between Kolkata and:
e: The Maitree Express runs between Kolkata and Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh, restoring direct rail passenger links between the two countries.

q: The Thar Express between Jodhpur and Karachi crossed the India-Pakistan border at:
e: The Thar Express between Jodhpur and Karachi crossed the India-Pakistan border at Munabao, with Khokhrapar being the corresponding station on the Pakistan side.

q: The New Pamban Bridge in Tamil Nadu is India's first railway sea bridge of which type?
e: The New Pamban Bridge in Tamil Nadu is India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge; its central lift span rises to allow ships to pass beneath.

q: In terms of the size of the rail network, Indian Railways ranks as the world's:
e: In terms of network size, Indian Railways ranks as the fourth largest rail network in the world, after the United States, China and Russia.

q: How many Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs) conduct recruitment for Indian Railways?
e: Recruitment to Indian Railways is conducted through 21 Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs) located in different parts of the country.

q: The 'Mountain Railways of India' inscribed by UNESCO as a single World Heritage property comprise:

options.A: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, Matheran Railway and Kangra Valley Railway
options.B: Nilgiri Mountain Railway, Kangra Valley Railway and Kalka-Shimla Railway
options.C: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, Nilgiri Mountain Railway and Kalka-Shimla Railway
options.D: Kalka-Shimla Railway, Matheran Railway and Nilgiri Mountain Railway

e: The UNESCO property "Mountain Railways of India" comprises three lines: the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, the Nilgiri Mountain Railway and the Kalka-Shimla Railway.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Konkan Railway:
1. Its route passes through the States of Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka.
2. The project was executed through a special purpose corporation, broadly on a Build-Operate-Transfer pattern.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Konkan Railway route passes through Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka along the west coast, and the project was executed through a special purpose corporation broadly on a Build-Operate-Transfer pattern.

q: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
e: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949; it came into force on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day.

q: The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India deals with:

options.A: The Union List, State List and Concurrent List
options.C: Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha

e: The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains the Union List, the State List and the Concurrent List, distributing legislative powers between the Union and the States.

q: The oath of office to the President of India is administered by the:
e: The oath of office to the President of India is administered by the Chief Justice of India, as provided in Article 60 of the Constitution.

q: The maximum permissible strength of the Rajya Sabha is:
e: The maximum permissible strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 members: up to 238 representing the States and Union Territories and 12 nominated by the President.

q: A Money Bill is defined in the Constitution under:
e: A Money Bill is defined in Article 110 of the Constitution, which specifies the matters that a Money Bill may exclusively deal with.

q: The concept of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of:
e: The concept of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland.

q: The first woman President of India was:
e: Pratibha Patil became the first woman President of India in 2007, succeeding Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

q: A joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament is presided over by the:
e: A joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament, summoned by the President to resolve a deadlock, is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

q: The first Speaker of the Lok Sabha was:
e: G. V. Mavalankar was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha, holding the office from 1952 until his death in 1956.

q: The Ninth Schedule was added to the Constitution by the:
e: The Ninth Schedule was added to the Constitution by the First Amendment Act of 1951, initially to protect land reform laws from judicial challenge.

q: The ancient city of Mohenjo-daro of the Indus Valley Civilisation was discovered by:
e: The ancient city of Mohenjo-daro of the Indus Valley Civilisation was discovered in 1922 by R. D. Banerji of the Archaeological Survey of India.

q: The Grand Trunk (GT) Road running from Kolkata to Peshawar was built by:
e: The Grand Trunk (GT) Road running from Kolkata to Peshawar was built in its historic form by Sher Shah Suri in the sixteenth century.

q: The edicts of Emperor Ashoka were first deciphered by:
e: The edicts of Emperor Ashoka, inscribed mainly in the Brahmi script, were first deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.

q: The Simon Commission arrived in India in the year:
e: The Simon Commission, an all-British body appointed to review constitutional reforms, arrived in India in 1928 and was greeted with widespread protests.

q: The Poona Pact of 1932 was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and:
e: The Poona Pact of 1932 was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, giving the Depressed Classes reserved seats within joint electorates instead of separate electorates.

q: The Cabinet Mission, which proposed a plan for the transfer of power, came to India in the year:
e: The Cabinet Mission, sent by the British Government to propose a plan for the transfer of power, came to India in 1946.

q: The first President of the Indian National Congress was:
e: W. C. Bonnerjee was the first President of the Indian National Congress, presiding over its founding session held at Bombay in 1885.

q: Mahatma Gandhi's first Satyagraha movement in India was launched at:
e: Mahatma Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India was launched at Champaran in Bihar in 1917, in support of the indigo cultivators against the planters.

q: The Arya Samaj was founded by:
e: The Arya Samaj was founded in 1875 by Swami Dayananda Saraswati, who preached a return to the Vedas through his work Satyarth Prakash.

q: The Battle of Talikota (1565) led to the fall of the:
e: The Battle of Talikota in 1565, in which the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates defeated Vijayanagara, led to the fall of the Vijayanagara Empire.

q: Majuli, the world's largest river island, is formed by the river:
e: Majuli, the world's largest river island, is formed by the Brahmaputra river in Assam and is a centre of Assamese Vaishnavite culture.

q: The Tehri Dam, one of the highest dams in India, is built across the river:
e: The Tehri Dam, one of the highest dams in India, is built across the Bhagirathi river in Uttarakhand.

q: The highest mountain peak situated in India is:
e: Kangchenjunga, rising 8,586 metres on the Sikkim-Nepal border, is the highest mountain peak situated in India; K2 lies in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.

q: The Palk Strait separates India from:
e: The Palk Strait separates India (Tamil Nadu coast) from Sri Lanka, lying between the two countries north of the Gulf of Mannar.

q: The Ten Degree Channel separates:

options.A: The Andaman group and the Nicobar group of islands

e: The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman group of islands from the Nicobar group in the Bay of Bengal, taking its name from the 10 degree north latitude.
